name: Val Evans
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember wearing a cloak held shut with washing pegs.” On Monday, near the blocks below Foundry Lofts, Val checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: I played the villain in the school production. I want a rematch in front of my own grandchildren.
appearance: Val has two dimples that appear only with a full smile. Look for short copper curls. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a moss-green cardigan with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. In conversation Val draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first.
personality: Val has a strong competitive streak and a very soft spot for the person finishing last. A prize tastes better when everybody had enough time to enter.
agenda: To perform the villain again for the grandchildren.
family: Jody Gomez is Val’s stepsibling. Val makes the call. Jody is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *Care with a clock*, Jody says, “I care for my uncle free. I'm learning what calling my labor free has cost my own pension.”
connections: Orla Jain. Sorting the box unearths the old school production remembered by its villain.

reactions.situation: A customer is short at the till while a queue forms
reactions.response: Val keeps the customer's place while they check the amount and gets the impatient people talking about something else.
